code.source:
import json
from pathlib import Path

FILE = Path("expenses.json")

def load():
    if not FILE.exists():
        return []
    return json.loads(FILE.read_text())

def save(items):
    FILE.write_text(json.dumps(items))

items = load()
print(len(items))
items.append({"category": "food", "cents": 12050})
save(items)
print(len(load()))

scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the Python error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. Point two nine times one hundred should be twenty nine. Python prints twenty eight. The float is a hair below point two nine, and int cuts off the end. A cent vanishes, and no error appears. Read money as text with Decimal instead, and the answer is exactly twenty nine.

props.why: Floats store point two nine as an approximation just below it, so multiplying and cutting off the end loses a cent. Decimal reads the text exactly.

shorts.title: Float trouble
